annotation_description: With a pure control hand containing only 1 land out of 7 cards (Floodfarm Verge, 2x Day of Judgment, Stock Up, Consult the Star Charts, Spell Snare, Three Steps Ahead), choosing to play first is debatable. Control decks with reactive game plans often benefit more from the extra card on the draw, and this hand desperately needs to find more lands. The extra draw step would significantly improve chances of hitting land drops to cast the expensive spells in hand.

With no lands in play on turn 2, paying 2 life for Hallowed Fountain to enter untapped is wasteful since they can't meaningfully use the mana this turn anyway (postcombat main, no 1-mana plays worth making). Playing Restless Anchorage tapped this turn costs nothing since it would be tapped regardless, and saves Hallowed Fountain for a later turn where entering untapped actually matters (e.g., turn 3 to hold up No More Lies).

Gem3F Valley has 7 cards in hand and 5 lands on the battlefield with an Undercity Sewers entering tapped on the stack. They have Demolition Field in hand but chose not to play it as their land drop for the turn. With 5 lands already (soon to be 6 with the Sewers resolving), playing Demolition Field would give them access to more mana and a useful utility land to threaten the opponent's nonbasic lands (like Hallowed Fountain or Sunken Citadel). Missing a land drop when holding a land is suboptimal, especially when the player has a hand full of reactive spells that benefit from having more mana available.

Gem3F Valley has 5 lands (one tapped), and it's the postcombat main phase of their own turn with the opponent tapped out (Sunken Citadel tapped). They could cast Consult the Star Charts (potentially kicked for 4 mana total) to dig for threats or answers, using mana that would otherwise go to waste. With 4 available mana (Gloomlake Verge, Swamp, Fountainport, Undercity Sewers untapped), they could cast the base Consult the Star Charts for 2 mana looking at 5 cards, or use Fountainport's abilities. Passing without using any mana on their own turn when they have card selection available is a missed opportunity, especially since they could hold up countermagic on the opponent's turn with remaining mana after casting Consult. However, they may want to hold up Three Steps Ahead (3 mana counter mode) plus Spell Snare, which is a reasonable defensive posture. The decision is close but passing up Consult the Star Charts when the opponent is tapped out seems like a missed opportunity to improve hand quality.

Gem25P Drama declined to cast Seam Rip with no apparent downside. With 4 lands (including tapped Restless Anchorage and Sunken Citadel), they have mana available to cast Seam Rip ({W}) while still holding up No More Lies ({W}{U}) on the opponent's turn. Seam Rip could exile a relevant nonland permanent with mana value 2 or less from the opponent's side - notably Fountainport, which is an important utility land that generates tokens and draws cards. Even if there's nothing critical to exile right now, declining to even consider it when the opponent has Fountainport on board (a nonland permanent with no mana value restriction... wait, Fountainport is a land, so it's not a valid target). Looking at the opponent's board: Gloomlake Verge (land), Swamp (land), Fountainport (land), Undercity Sewers x2 (lands) - all lands, no nonland permanents. So Seam Rip actually has no valid targets currently. The decision to pass is reasonable in that case. However, the player could have played one of their two Fountainports from hand as a land drop if they hadn't already made one this turn. Actually, reviewing the board state more carefully - it's postcombat main, and their lands suggest they may have already played a land this turn (4 lands on board). The pass seems fine.

At end of turn (postcombat main, about to pass), Gem3F Valley has 5 lands and Consult the Star Charts in hand with mana available. This is a prime opportunity to use mana at end of opponent's turn to dig for threats or answers. Passing with mana up when holding a card-selection instant wastes the mana. While holding up Three Steps Ahead for countermagic is reasonable, they have TWO copies of Three Steps Ahead plus two Spell Snares, so they have plenty of countermagic already. Using Consult the Star Charts (2 mana) while keeping 3 mana up for Three Steps Ahead would have been optimal - they could look at 5 cards and find a better card while still maintaining counter protection.

Gem3F Valley passed with 6 mana available and Consult the Star Charts in hand. Casting it for {1}{U} would look at the top 6 cards and put the best one in hand, while still leaving 4 mana open - enough to cast Three Steps Ahead's counter mode ({1}{U}{U} = 3 mana) or Spell Snare ({U}). The hand is entirely reactive with no win condition, making card selection valuable to find threats or lands.

With 6 lands in play and the opponent tapped out (Restless Anchorage is tapped, Sunken Citadel enters tapped), this was an excellent opportunity to use Consult the Star Charts to dig 6 cards deep for additional resources, or to use Demolition Field to destroy Restless Anchorage (a dangerous manland) or Sunken Citadel while the opponent can't respond meaningfully. Passing with 6 mana available and no pressing reason to hold up all of it wastes tempo. While holding up countermagic (Three Steps Ahead, Spell Snare) has value, using Consult the Star Charts at end of opponent's turn would have been better than doing nothing, and the opponent is largely tapped out anyway.

Gem3F Valley has 6 lands in play and 6 mana available, with Demolition Field able to destroy Restless Anchorage (a key threat that becomes a 2/3 flyer and generates Map tokens). The opponent only has 4 lands with Restless Anchorage being their only nonbasic land worth targeting. Using Demolition Field now would remove a significant threat while both players search for basics - Valley has plenty of lands already and the opponent is land-light. Additionally, Fountainport could create a Fish token (3 mana + 1 life) or a Treasure token (4 mana) as a mana sink, though these are less urgent. Consult the Star Charts could also be cast at end of opponent's turn instead, so passing main phase is not necessarily wrong for that card.

chosen_display: 3. {1}{W}{U}: Until end of turn, Restless Anchorage becomes a 2/3 white and blue Bird creature with flying. It's still a land.
annotation_description: Activating Restless Anchorage to attack on turn 7 with only 4 lands (one of which is now tapped as a creature) while the opponent has 6 lands open and a full hand is risky but potentially reasonable as chip damage. However, the real concern is sequencing: Drama has Elspeth, Storm Slayer in hand (5 mana) and two Fountainports to play. By animating Restless Anchorage and using 3 mana (1WU) to do so, Drama is left with only 1 untapped land after combat, making it impossible to hold up No More Lies or cast anything meaningful post-combat. If Drama instead played a land first (Fountainport or Demolition Field) and then decided whether to animate, they'd have more options. Additionally, attacking into an opponent with 6 open mana and unknown cards could walk into removal, though the opponent is playing UB which has limited instant-speed interaction with a 2/3 flyer.

Activating Restless Anchorage before playing a land from hand. With two Fountainports in hand, playing one first would give an extra untapped land, allowing them to hold up No More Lies (WU) after the Anchorage activation. By activating first, they spend 3 of 5 mana and may not have enough left to both play a land and hold up countermagic optimally.

Gem25P Drama has a Map Token on the battlefield that could be activated as a sorcery-speed ability to let a creature explore (draw/filter). However, they have no creatures on the battlefield to target with the Map Token, so that specific activation isn't available. More importantly, they have Sunken Citadel untapped which could generate mana, and they could potentially use Fountainport (if they played one) to create tokens or draw cards. The real miss here is not playing a land - they have two Fountainports in hand and appear to have not played a land this turn (all their lands from prior turns are accounted for). Playing Fountainport would give them an additional mana source and a mana sink for future turns. While they may have played a land earlier in the turn (the action log is incomplete), if they haven't, missing this land drop with Fountainport in hand is a clear mistake.

In a control mirror, letting opponent's card selection spell (Consult the Star Charts) resolve when holding Spell Snare, which perfectly answers it at 1 mana. Spell Snare is narrow and may not find a better 2-mana target, and letting the opponent dig through 5 cards for free gives them incremental advantage in the mirror.

Activating Restless Anchorage before playing a land for the turn. Drama has Restless Anchorage and Fountainport in hand and hasn't made a land drop yet. While the opponent is tapped out making the attack itself correct, playing a land first (either one, since both are relevant) ensures the land drop isn't forgotten and could matter for available mana later.

Gem25P Drama has Fountainport untapped and 2 Map tokens on the battlefield. They could sacrifice a Map token to Fountainport's ability ({2}, {T}, Sacrifice a token: Draw a card) to draw a card at end of opponent's combat step, using mana from Sunken Citadel. This is a pure-upside mana sink that generates card advantage at no real cost since they have excess tokens and available mana. The Sunken Citadel can produce 2 mana for land abilities, which exactly pays the {2} activation cost of Fountainport.

Missed opportunity to activate Fountainport's draw ability ({2}, {T}, Sacrifice a token: Draw a card) using Sunken Citadel's 2 mana (for land abilities) and sacrificing one of the Map tokens. With no creatures on board, the Map tokens have minimal value, making this essentially a free card draw.

Gem3F Valley is a control deck with 8 cards in hand (over the maximum hand size of 7) and 6 lands in play. Casting Stock Up (a sorcery) during their main phase taps 3 mana and draws 2 cards, bringing them to 9 cards in hand, meaning they'll need to discard 2 at end of turn. While they do need to find answers, they already have a very full hand with counterspells, removal, and board wipes. Spending mana on their own turn for a sorcery-speed card advantage spell when they're already going to discard is wasteful - they're essentially spending 3 mana to upgrade 1 card (draw 2, discard 2 net from the Stock Up + end of turn discard). They could instead hold up countermagic and removal with their 6 mana, and use Demolition Field to destroy the opponent's Fountainport or Sunken Citadel at end of turn if mana is unused, or activate Fountainport to make a fish/treasure at end of opponent's turn.

Activating Restless Anchorage before playing their land for the turn (Fountainport in hand). Playing the land first would provide an additional mana source, leaving 4 mana open after animating Anchorage instead of 3, giving more flexibility to hold up interaction like No More Lies plus additional mana.

Gem25P Drama has Fountainport in hand but declined to play it, missing their land drop for the turn. In a control mirror at turn 10, having an additional land (7th land) is significant for activating Restless Anchorage, holding up multiple counterspells, or using Fountainport's abilities.

Gem25P Drama skipped their entire combat phase without attacking with Restless Anchorage, which could have been animated for 1WU to become a 2/3 flyer. They had the mana available (Hallowed Fountain, Plains, Sunken Citadel, Demolition Field, Fountainport are untapped lands) to activate Restless Anchorage and attack for 2 flying damage plus create a Map token. The opponent has no creatures to block a flyer. Over multiple turns, this represents significant missed damage and card quality from Map tokens. The player's reasoning incorrectly dismissed the combat step prompt as irrelevant, failing to recognize they should animate and attack with their creature-land.

Failed to animate and attack with Restless Anchorage during their own combat phase. The opponent has no creatures to block, and a 2/3 flyer would deal 2 damage (opponent at 16 life) while creating a Map token for card selection. There's no meaningful risk since the opponent has no board presence.

In a control mirror with no opposing creatures, declining to attack with Restless Anchorage (2/3 flyer) means missing 2 damage and a Map token. However, activating it would leave no blue mana to hold up No More Lies against potential threats from the opponent's 7 open mana.

Instead they passed without using the mana sink, wasting an opportunity to convert a spare token into card advantage.

The 2 life payment is unnecessary when the board is a grindy control mirror and life is a resource. They could have let it enter tapped and still had 7 mana available, which is more than enough to hold up No More Lies and still cast Stock Up or other spells.

With Hallowed Fountain, Plains, Sunken Citadel, and Demolition Field still untapped, they had enough mana to activate Fountainport (2 generic + tap) and still hold up No More Lies ({W}{U}) with their remaining lands. Drawing an extra card in a control mirror is meaningful value.

With 7 lands available and the opponent tapped out (Restless Anchorage is tapped, suggesting they attacked or activated it), this was an opportunity to deploy Wan Shi Tong, Librarian at end of opponent's turn or during main phase. Casting Wan Shi Tong for X=5 (7 mana total) would create a 6/6 flyer with vigilance and draw 2 cards, establishing a significant clock and card advantage. The opponent has no creatures on board and limited ability to deal with a large flyer. Valley has 7 lands but only passed, missing the chance to use mana productively. While holding up countermagic is reasonable, Valley already has Essence Scatter, Spell Pierce, and two Three Steps Ahead - deploying a threat while still being able to hold up some interaction next turn would be stronger than doing nothing with all mana.

Casting Day of Judgment when there are zero creatures on the battlefield. This wastes a powerful board wipe and 4 mana for absolutely no effect. The opponent has no creatures, and the player has no creatures either - the spell accomplishes literally nothing.

Cast Day of Judgment when there are zero creatures on the battlefield. Restless Reef is a land (its animation from opponent's previous turn has worn off), so the board wipe destroys nothing. This wastes a critical board wipe that could answer future creature threats like Wan Shi Tong.

The opponent has no flying blockers (Restless Reef is a 4/4 deathtouch without flying), so the Anchorage would deal 2 unblockable damage and create a Map token. However, discarding Hallowed Fountain is reasonable since they already have sufficient lands on the battlefield.

Missing 2 damage and a Map token in a close game (opponent at 16 life) is significant.
